rules.title: npm package is incompatible with this platform
rules.summary: npm rejected a package because its declared operating-system, CPU-architecture, or libc constraints do not match the current environment.
rules.root_cause: The package (or one of its dependencies) declares platform constraints that exclude the environment in which npm is running.
checks: Confirm the environment with `node --version`, `npm --version`, and `node -p "process.platform + ' ' + process.arch"`.
Identify the exact package named near the EBADPLATFORM message; do not assume the top-level package is responsible.
Inspect that package's published `os`, `cpu`, and `libc` metadata and its documented supported platforms.
actions: Choose a package release that explicitly supports this operating system and architecture, or use the vendor-documented alternative for this platform.
If the project is running inside a container, WSL, Termux, or an emulator, verify that Node.js reports the platform you expect.
Avoid using `--force` as a first response: it can bypass compatibility checks without making the package work.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; package-specific compatibility must be verified against the package's current metadata.

rules.title: npm could not resolve the dependency tree
rules.summary: npm found peer-dependency requirements that cannot all be satisfied by the versions currently selected.
rules.root_cause: Two or more packages request incompatible peer-dependency ranges, or the project's installed dependency set conflicts with its manifest.
checks: Read the full ERESOLVE report and note the packages listed as `Found` and `Could not resolve dependency`.
Compare the peer-dependency ranges in the involved packages' published metadata.
Check whether package.json and the lockfile describe the same intended dependency set.
actions: Select mutually compatible package versions and update the manifest and lockfile together.
Upgrade or replace the package whose peer range conflicts with the rest of the application.
Do not default to `--force` or `--legacy-peer-deps`; those flags can hide a dependency conflict rather than resolve it.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; the specific version conflict must be checked in the project's dependency graph.

rules.title: Python cannot find an imported module
rules.summary: The active Python interpreter cannot resolve a module requested by an import statement.
rules.root_cause: The dependency may be missing from the active environment, installed for a different interpreter, or imported under a different distribution/module name.
checks: Confirm which interpreter is running with `python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"`.
Check the active environment with `python -m pip show <distribution-name>`.
Compare the import name with the package's documented installation name; they are not always identical.
actions: Install the missing distribution into the same interpreter/environment that runs the program, preferably inside a project virtual environment.
If a virtual environment is intended, activate it and repeat the interpreter and package checks.
For a project, add the dependency to its declared dependency file so collaborators can reproduce the environment.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; the missing module and interpreter must be confirmed locally.

rules.title: pip cannot find a compatible dependency set
rules.summary: pip's resolver cannot find versions that satisfy all declared constraints for the requested packages and Python environment.
rules.root_cause: Pinned versions, transitive requirements, Python-version constraints, or platform-specific wheels may be mutually incompatible.
checks: Read the resolver's conflict report and identify the exact packages and version ranges it names.
Check Python version and platform compatibility for each required package.
Review direct pins and constraints files before changing transitive dependencies.
actions: Relax or update only the constraints that are genuinely incompatible, then resolve and test the complete environment again.
Prefer a supported package release for the current Python version rather than forcing an incompatible install.
Record the resulting dependency set in the project's standard lock or requirements workflow.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; exact package compatibility requires a resolver run in the target environment.

rules.title: Python environment is externally managed
rules.summary: The operating system marks its Python installation as externally managed and blocks package changes through the system interpreter.
rules.root_cause: The Python installation is managed by the operating system package manager, which protects system-owned packages from conflicting pip modifications.
checks: Confirm whether the interpreter belongs to the operating system or a project virtual environment.
Check whether the distribution recommends its package manager for system-wide Python packages.
actions: Create and activate a project virtual environment, then install project dependencies inside it.
Use the operating system package manager for packages intended to be installed system-wide.
Avoid bypassing the externally-managed protection unless you fully understand the system-level consequences.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; the environment manager must be identified on the affected machine.

rules.title: Git command was run outside a repository
rules.summary: Git cannot find repository metadata in the current directory or any parent directory.
rules.root_cause: The shell is in the wrong directory, the repository has not been cloned or initialized, or the expected .git metadata is absent.
match_any: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories)
checks: Print the current directory with `pwd` (or `Get-Location` in PowerShell).
List the directory contents and confirm that it is the project root.
Check whether the project contains a `.git` directory or worktree metadata.
actions: Change into the existing cloned repository directory and retry the Git command.
If the project has never been cloned, clone the intended remote first.
Initialize a new repository only when this directory is meant to become a new Git project.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; the correct project directory is environment-specific.

rules.title: Git SSH authentication was rejected
rules.summary: The SSH server did not accept a public key offered by the local SSH client.
rules.root_cause: The expected key may not be loaded, may not be registered with the Git hosting account, or the remote may use a different account or host alias.
checks: Inspect the remote URL with `git remote -v` and confirm that it points to the expected host and account.
Check which public keys are loaded using `ssh-add -l`; never paste or share a private key.
Run the hosting provider's documented SSH connection test and read the account name in the response.
actions: Register the intended public key with the correct hosting account, or load the intended key into the SSH agent.
Correct an outdated remote URL if it points to the wrong host or account.
If SSH is not required, use the provider's documented HTTPS remote method instead.

references.label: GitHub: adding a new SSH key

rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; authentication must be tested against the user's own account.

rules.title: The linker cannot find a referenced symbol
rules.summary: Compilation reached the linking stage, but the linker could not find a definition for one or more referenced symbols.
rules.root_cause: A required source file or library may be missing from the link command, a function signature may not match, or the library order may be incorrect for the selected linker.
checks: Confirm whether every declared function has a matching definition in a compiled source file or linked library.
Inspect the full compile-and-link command, not only the final error line.
Check C/C++ linkage and library ordering where relevant to the toolchain.
actions: Include the source file that defines the missing symbol in the build target.
Link the required library using the compiler driver's documented options and ordering.
For C++ projects, verify namespace, overload, and `extern "C"` boundaries before changing linker flags.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; the exact missing symbol must be traced in the target build.

rules.title: Gradle could not resolve a dependency
rules.summary: Gradle could not locate or select a dependency version required by a project configuration.
rules.root_cause: The dependency coordinates may be incorrect, the repository may be missing, credentials may be unavailable, or version constraints may conflict.
match_any: Could not resolve all files for configuration
checks: Identify the exact dependency coordinates and configuration named in the failure.
Confirm that the required Maven repository is declared and reachable from the build environment.
Check whether the requested artifact version actually exists and supports the project's Java/Gradle versions.
actions: Correct the dependency coordinates or version using the library's official publication information.
Add the required repository only when it is a trusted source for that dependency.
Resolve authentication or proxy configuration issues without committing credentials to the repository.
rules.verification: Rule signature and registry tests are covered by the local test suite; repository reachability and artifact availability are environment-dependent.
